sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Retail Sale via Automated Dropshipping Networks

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state tax or commercial-law distinctions applicable)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic tradition; unitary national legal system; EU directives and regulations directly applicable; French and German commercial law influences consolidated in the Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: China–Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) Bilateral Investment Treaty (2005, in force since 1 December 2009)
EU–China Comprehensive Agreement on Investment (signed 30 December 2020; not yet in force)
Luxembourg–United States Double Taxation Agreement (signed 3 April 1996, as amended by Protocols of 2004 and 2009)
Luxembourg–Germany Double Taxation Agreement (treaty of 23 August 1958, as amended by subsequent protocols)
Luxembourg–France Double Taxation Agreement (treaty of 1 April 1958, as amended by subsequent protocols)
Luxembourg–People's Republic of China Double Taxation Agreement (signed 12 March 1994, as amended by the 2020 amending protocol)
Luxembourg–Netherlands Double Taxation Agreement (1968, as amended)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Principal legal instruments: (1) Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing ('AML/CFT Law of 2004'), as amended, including by the Law of 25 March 2020 transposing Directive (EU) 2018/843 (AMLD5); (2) Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners ('RBE Law'), as amended by the Law of 25 March 2020; (3) Grand-Ducal Regulation of 19 May 2020 on the organisational and operational modalities of the RBE; (4) Law of 19 December 2020 on financial sanctions and the freezing of funds; (5) CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on AML/CFT, together with CSSF Circular 18/656 and Circular 20/744; (6) Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, Title III as introduced by the Law of 23 July 2016 creating the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp) (Articles 1-2 and 907-926); (7) CRF (Cellule de Renseignement Financier) reporting regime and CSSF guidance on beneficial ownership. Following the CJEU judgments in C-37/20 and C-601/20 (WM and Sovim, 2022), Luxembourg restricted public access to the RBE; access now covers competent authorities, obliged entities carrying out AML due diligence, and persons demonstrating a legitimate interest in a specific legal entity.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / excerpt from the commercial register of the foreign corporate general partner (proving corporate existence and incumbency)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of the corporate partner's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961 Hague Apostille Convention — Luxembourg is a Contracting State) OR Consular Legalization via the Luxembourg embassy/consulate for non-Contracting States

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney authorizing the founding signatory and the Luxembourg submitting agent to execute and file the SCSp constitutional deed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the partner's home state, followed by apostille or consular legalization before the Luxembourg consular post
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization (notarial act must first be legalized by the competent authority of the origin state before apostille or Luxembourg consular legalization)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies and proof of residential address for each natural-person UBO and the designated gérant
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent public authority or licensed certifier in the country of origin; underlying notarization required before apostille or legalization
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization (certified copies must be notarized in the origin state, then apostilled or legalized by the Luxembourg consular post)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds declaration for the initial capital contribution of each partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Correspondent bank or licensed credit institution holding the contribution, with signature authenticated by a notary of the origin state
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization where the bank or notary requires independent authentication; otherwise the bank letter must be apostilled/legalized only if presented to Luxembourg public authorities in original certified form

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based CDD under Articles 3, 5 and 8 of the AML/CFT Law of 2004 and CSSF Regulation 12-02: all UBOs and the gérant must be screened at origination, on any change of control, and at least annually. PEP status is defined by Article 2(2)(14°) of the AML/CFT Law of 2004 (foreign PEPs included; domestic PEP exposure assessed on a risk-sensitive basis). Screening must be run against: (i) the EU Commission Consolidated Financial Sanctions Database (FISC), (ii) the UN Security Council consolidated lists (1267/1989 and 1988 regimes), (iii) the Luxembourg national financial-sanctions list of the Ministry of Finance, and (iv) OFAC's SDN and SSI lists — OFAC being applied as a best-practice control given anticipated USD settlement via Stripe and PayPal rails. A confirmed PEP or sanctions hit triggers: enhanced due diligence, written senior-management approval, verification of source of funds and source of wealth, immediate asset-freeze reporting to the CRF under the Law of 19 December 2020, and, where applicable, advisory filing under CSSF Circular 20/744. Screening results must be documented in the AML/CFT file and retained for at least five years after the business relationship ends.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); electronic filing portal: https://www.lbr.lu and the LODT/RCS e-deposit module ('dépôt électronique')
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: RCS filings are accepted in French, German or Luxembourgish; French is the customary operative language and the prudent default for non-fluent founders. The company name must be expressed in the Latin alphabet with full diacritical fidelity. A corporate name containing non-Latin script elements (e.g., Cyrillic or CJK characters) must be accompanied by a Latin-script transliteration and a sworn French translation; the Latin-script version becomes the sole operative RCS name. The name must be distinctive, non-misleading, and not identical or confusingly similar to existing RCS registrations or to trademarks protected in Luxembourg and at the European Union Intellectual Property Office (EUIPO); statutory suffixes (SA, Sàrl, SCA, SECS) may not be used unless the constitutional instrument actually adopts the corresponding legal form.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: banque / bank / bancaire — prior authorisation of the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) required
assurance / réassurance / insurance — prior authorisation of the Commissariat aux Assurances (CAA) required
fonds de placement / OPC / OPCVM / SICAV / SICAF — prior CSSF authorisation required
bourse / société de bourse / marché réglementé — prior CSSF authorisation required
fiduciaire / trust — reserved for CSSF-licensed professional fiduciary companies; not available to an SCSp
état / national / gouvernemental / royal — misleading sovereign or public connotation; ministerial approval required
université / académie / école — concurrence of the Ministry of Education required
coopérative — restricted to entities genuinely constituted as cooperatives under Title II of the Law of 10 August 1915
AMAZON / EBAY / ALIEXPRESS / PAYPAL / SHOPIFY — protected third-party trademarks and descriptive marketplace descriptors that may trigger EUIPO infringement objections
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The RCS name-reservation window is strictly 30 days and is non-extendable; on expiry the name returns to public availability and a fresh reservation request must be submitted. Rejection procedure: (1) within five business days of refusal the filing party obtains the LBR's written opinion stating the refusal ground; (2) an administrative reconsideration request is submitted through the notary or registered agent within 15 days of the written refusal; (3) if reconsideration fails, a petition may be filed with the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (commercial chamber) by a Luxembourg-qualified avocat à la Cour, invoking the 'identical or confusingly similar' standard of the RCS rules; (4) an appeal from the court's judgment lies to the Luxembourg Court of Appeal within 40 days of notification. As a risk management practice, the incorporator should reserve two to three fallback names in parallel so the RBE/UBO filing timeline is not delayed by an appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the statutory seat. An SCSp must have a real physical registered office in Luxembourg (Article 1-2 and 907 of the Law of 10 August 1915, as amended by the Law of 23 July 2016). The RCS will not accept a PO Box, a virtual address, or a mail-forwarding-only address as the siège social. However, the prevailing market practice is the use of a CSSF-licensed domiciliation agent or société fiduciaire, which supplies a physical Luxembourg suite, mail handling and a compliant service-of-process address. For tax-transparent SCSp structures, Luxembourg tax residence is not presumed from the registered office alone; if central administration and management functions remain outside Luxembourg, the SCSp will be treated as tax-resident in the partners' jurisdiction under applicable double taxation principles, and the Luxembourg substance should be limited to the registered office and statutory filings.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: 30–35% likelihood of an unannounced physical inspection by the CSSF or the CRF within the first 12 months for a medium-risk enhanced automated-dropshipping entity. Triggering factors that materially raise the risk: registration at a shared domiciliation address hosting more than 20 unrelated entities, absence or prolonged delay in opening a bank account, turnover disproportionate to declared substance, incomplete or late RBE registration, or counterparties appearing on adverse-media or sanctions watchlists. Inspections are conducted under the AML/CFT Law of 2004 and CSSF Regulation 12-02; on-site inspectors verify governance, source-of-funds documentation, UBO files and administrative reality.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Statutory company-name search, RCS/LBR negative-name certificate and name reservation handling
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), name verification department
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff (approx. EUR 15 certificate issuance per Grand-Ducal Regulation of 20 April 2006, as amended) plus prevailing market benchmark of EUR 90–150 registered-agent handling fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting and legal review of the SCSp limited partnership agreement (acte de société / convention de commandite spéciale) and general-partner constitutional review
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg law firm (avocat à la Cour) and, if notarial form is preferred, a Luxembourg notary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark: EUR 1,800–2,800 flat fee for a standard single-purpose SCSp; notarial deed option adds approximately EUR 800–1,500 per statutory notary tariff

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended; Articles 944-1 to 944-12 (SCSp regime) inserted by the Law of 12 July 2013; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies and the annual accounts of undertakings.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), in coordination with the RCS Section of the District Court of Luxembourg.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Registration application with the RCS (formulaire de demande d'inscription au RCS) accompanied by the notarized or privately signed limited partnership agreement (contrat de société) and the declaration of appointment of the manager.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The SCSp has no statutory minimum capital and no escrow account requirement; partners may contribute on a purely deferred basis, and the partnership agreement freely determines capital, capital calls, and profit-sharing ratios.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the subscribers be, and hereby are, admitted as the sole general partner and limited partner(s), each subscribing to the interests set forth in the limited partnership agreement; that the registered office be established at [ADDRESS], Luxembourg; that [NAME] be appointed Manager (Gérant) with full power to represent the Partnership and execute all banking, contractual, and regulatory filings; that the Manager be authorized to open bank accounts, engage auditors and tax advisors, and complete registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers and revenue authorities; and that all prior acts performed in the Partnership's name be ratified and confirmed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the SCSp Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary of the Luxembourg District Court (required only where contributions consist of real estate; otherwise private deed) and the founding partners.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare a comprehensive partnership agreement (English or French) containing the corporate name, registered office address, corporate purpose limited to authorized e-commerce and dropshipping activities, contribution schedule, identity of the general partner and limited partner(s), profit-sharing rules, manager appointment clause, and dissolution terms. Execute a private deed (acte sous seing privé) or notarial deed if a real estate contribution is made. Obtain a Luxembourg LEI code for the SCSp and verified identity documents for the ultimate beneficial owners.
required_dossiers: Identity documents (passport) and proof of residence of all partners and the manager
Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) disclosure forms
Bank reference letters and CVs of the manager
Draft limited partnership agreement
Business plan and economic substance documentation for e-commerce activity
LEI application form or existing LEI certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or the bank queries identity or source-of-funds documentation, submit apostilled or certified true copies within 15 days; if the corporate purpose is too broad, amend the draft deed before signature and re-execute without additional notarial cost.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS Registration Filing Through Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) electronic portal (www.lbr.lu / MyGuichet.lu), RCS section.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the standardized RCS registration application electronically, attaching the executed partnership agreement, identification of the SCSp's registered office, appointment of the manager, and statement of the subscribed capital (even if zero). Pay the statutory filing fee by direct debit or payment instrument accepted on MyGuichet. The application must be filed by authorized counsel or the manager with a power of attorney.
required_dossiers: Signed and dated SCSp partnership agreement
RCS application form (form code A for commercial companies)
Identification and LEI of the SCSp and of the manager
Power of attorney, if filed through a Luxembourg counsel
Consent of the registered-office domiciliation agent (if any)
Payment receipt for the registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query regarding missing LEI, inconsistent corporate purpose, or defective mailing address, remedy by uploading a corrected slip and amended documents through the LBR portal within one month; contested refusals may be appealed to the Chamber of Commerce of the District Court of Luxembourg (Tribunal d'arrondissement).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Electronic Compendium of Companies and Associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RESA publication service.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful RCS registration, request the mandatory legal publicity in the RESA electronic gazette containing the statutory particulars of the SCSp: legal form, corporate name, registered office, registered capital, and the name and powers of the manager. The publication is executed automatically by the LBR in coordination with the RCS; no separate payment is required beyond the initial filing fee.
required_dossiers: RCS registration number
Excerpt of the RCS registration
Final approved partnership agreement
Publication request form processed by the LBR
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RESA publication is delayed or contains inaccurate particulars, file a corrective form and request rectification through the LBR helpdesk within 10 business days; retroactive effect of publication is preserved where the error is attributable to the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VAT Registration and E-Commerce One-Stop-Shop (OSS) Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) – Luxembourg Indirect Tax Authority, via MyGuichet.lu.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Luxembourg VAT registration application (form 640) to obtain a LU VAT number. For distance sales of imported goods below €150, register for the Union OSS or Import OSS scheme to declare VAT on dropshipping transaction flows across the EU. Select the tax regime appropriate to electronic retail, and settle the AEDT electronic communications requirement for invoicing.
required_dossiers: RCS certificate of registration (extrait du RCS)
Partnership agreement and manager identification
Form 640 – VAT registration with AEDT
E-services form for AEDT electronic correspondence
Expected annual turnover statement and country-by-country sales projection
Bank account details for the VAT refund mechanism
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEDT queries the place of supply or OSS eligibility, provide supplementary sales evidence and marketplace contracts within 20 days; appeals of VAT registration refusals lie to the Director of AEDT and subsequently to the Administrative Tribunal of Luxembourg.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and AML/KYC Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (e.g., bank or PFS/e-money institution) supervised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a professional operating bank account in the name of the SCSp to receive Stripe and PayPal settlements. Submit the full corporate kit, UBO declarations, economic substance evidence, and the pipeline transaction flow. Satisfy the institution's enhanced due diligence for medium-risk e-commerce activities, and arrange authorization for payment aggregators to settle funds directly into the SCSp account.
required_dossiers: RCS excerpt and certificate of good standing
Certified passport copies of the manager and all UBOs
Beneficial ownership register statement
Business plan, projected cash flows, and dropshipping marketplace agreements
Stripe/PayPal account structures and expected settlement volumes
Lease or domiciliation agreement for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the application on AML grounds, remedy by delivering a clarificatory economic-substance memorandum and revised source-of-funds documentation; a formal refusal letter may be challenged through the CSSF complaint mechanism and, ultimately, in the administrative courts.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy (Ministère de l'Économie) – Directorate for Industry, together with the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) for workplace-related permits.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating license required – automated dropshipping is an administrative and digital activity outside the scope of the Law of 2 September 2011 on the regulation of certain commercial activities; no commercial establishment permit (autorisation d'établissement) is triggered.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency), under the Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Category 3 (no EIA report and no registration) under the Law of 15 June 2018 on the environmental impact assessment of projects, because the SCSp carries no industrial facility, hazardous installation, or storage site; purely administrative e-commerce and remote dropshipping activities are below all EIA screening thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to the virtual operations; however, to the extent the SCSp imports physical goods into the EU, it must comply with the EU Packaging and Packaging Waste Directive (94/62/EC), the WEEE Directive (2012/19/EU), and the RoHS Directive (2011/65/EU) registration obligations through PRO environments, along with the Regulation on the Shipment of Waste for any returned or destroyed inventory.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification for the Luxembourg registered office obtained from the municipal fire brigade (CGDIS) where the office is physically open; workplace safety and structural load inspection clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) under the Law of 17 June 1994 on safety and health at work; because dropshipping automation does not involve warehouses or manufacturing, no industrial site clearance, pollution permit, or explosives authorization is required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED) for VAT and registration duties; unified e-filing portal at MyGuichet.lu (guichet.lu); direct tax forms via ACD, VAT forms and EC Sales Lists via the AED's e-service portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Register the SCSp and its managed entity in the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) to obtain the Luxembourg business registration number (numéro de matricule); 2) open a Luxembourg tax file with the ACD by submitting the partnership's constitutive deed, RCS extract, and partner identification, whereupon a Luxembourg direct-tax number is allocated; 3) file the VAT registration application (Déclaration d'assujettissement à la TVA) through MyGuichet/AED e-services supported by the matricule, proof of the automated dropshipping activity, and business premises or power of attorney; 4) the AED issues the LU+8 digit VAT identification number, typically within 2 to 4 weeks; 5) non-EU-established principals must appoint a Luxembourg VAT fiscal representative, while EU-established remote sellers may instead use the Luxembourg One-Stop-Shop (OSS) or Import One-Stop-Shop (IOSS) registration route; 6) obtain a Luxembourg EORI number prior to any customs export declaration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible - The SCSp is a fiscally transparent partnership by default: it has no legal personality and is not subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax or municipal business tax; profits, losses, and tax attributes flow through to partners in accordance with the partnership agreement. Although transparent for income tax, an SCSp carrying on a commercial automated dropshipping trade is itself a taxable person for Luxembourg VAT purposes and must register, charge, and reclaim VAT in its own name. The activity may also create a Luxembourg permanent establishment for foreign partners, exposing them to Luxembourg income tax on attributable profits.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg has no US-style check-the-box election. Statutory elections relevant to an SCSp include: (i) the irrevocable opt-in regime under Article 175 LIR (Luxembourg Income Tax Law) whereby an eligible transparent partnership may elect to be treated as a fully taxable capital company for corporate income tax and municipal business tax purposes; (ii) the VAT small-business exemption election under Article 57 of the Luxembourg VAT Law for taxable persons with annual turnover not exceeding EUR 35,000; (iii) designation of a Luxembourg VAT fiscal representative or agent; (iv) the OSS and IOSS registration elections for cross-border B2C and import supplies; and (v) written partnership profit- and loss-allocation elections, including special allocations, which the ACD follows provided partner-level reporting under the transparency regime is correct. Hybrid mismatch consequences are imposed automatically by the ATAD 2 provisions and cannot be altered by unilateral partner elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT/TVA - Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée) under the Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979 as amended; standard rate 17% effective 1 January 2025 (16% before that date); reduced rates of 14%, 8%, and 3% apply to specified goods and services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Domestic Luxembourg small-business VAT exemption: annual taxable turnover not exceeding EUR 35,000 (election available). A foreign non-established supplier has no de minimis exemption and must register from the first taxable Luxembourg supply. Intra-EU distance sales of goods by an EU-established supplier are subject to an EU-wide EUR 10,000 annual threshold, above which Luxembourg OSS registration is mandatory. Imported goods in consignments with intrinsic value not exceeding EUR 150 may be declared via IOSS; higher-value imports require standard Luxembourg VAT registration or the appointment of a customs agent.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not currently impose real-time fiscal clearance, API-connected digital stamping, or mandatory continuous transaction control (CTC) clearance for domestic B2B/B2C invoicing. E-invoicing is permitted, and EU Directive 2006/112/EC-compliant invoices must contain the statutory numbering and VAT details. VAT returns, EC Sales Lists (VIES), and Intrastat declarations are filed electronically via the MyGuichet/AED portal. The EU ViDA reform will introduce structured e-invoicing and digital tax reporting in Luxembourg in the upcoming legislative cycles; automated dropshipping platforms should nevertheless be configured now to issue compliant invoices and maintain audit-proof export documentation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% VAT rate applies to exports of goods physically consigned or transported outside the European Union by the supplier or by a third party on its behalf, provided the goods leave EU customs territory within the statutory time limit, generally 90 days, and the supplier obtains complete export evidence. For automated dropshipping, zero-rating requires that each shipment be linked to a valid Luxembourg/EU customs export declaration, shipping and transport documents proving actual exit, and the customer's non-EU status. Supplies of goods to EU VAT-registered customers are zero-rated as intra-Community supplies only where the customer's valid EU VAT ID is obtained and an EC Sales List is filed; automated B2C EU deliveries without OSS registration must be fully taxed at the Luxembourg rate. Digital and other B2B services generally follow the reverse-charge principle in the customer's EU jurisdiction and do not qualify as Luxembourg exports unless place-of-supply evidence under the B2B rules is obtained.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/e-DPE) with customs office exit confirmation (IE599 electronic export movement)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (B/L or AWB) evidencing carriage out of the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate and bank transfer evidence of FX repatriation from the foreign buyer
Commercial invoice, packing list, and order/dropshipping log linking the sale to the export declaration
Transport contracts, CMR waybills, or courier tracking movement proof
EORI number and customs broker mandate where the SCSp authorizes indirect representation
VAT export evidence register and partner/management declaration on the factual export chain
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is audited strictly by the AED and Luxembourg Customs: the taxpayer bears the burden of proof and must retain the complete export and remittance dossier, ordinarily for at least 10 years. Incorrect zero-rating is clawed back retrospectively with statutory late-payment interest, administrative fines which may reach up to 200% of the evaded VAT in fraud cases, and criminal liability including imprisonment and fines for fraudulent export schemes. In an automated dropshipping model, missing shipment-level proof, fictitious customs movements, or non-repatriated export proceeds trigger reversal of input VAT credits, denial of the 0% rate, and joint and several liability of the SCSp's managers and fiscal agents. Coordinated ACD/AED/Customs audits and EU administrative cooperation (DAC/DAC7) scrutiny of offshore buyers are standard in Luxembourg.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) together with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for banking and foreign exchange related prudential matters
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a member of the Eurozone and applies full current and capital account convertibility pursuant to the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and the EU Capital Movements Directive. There are no exchange control restrictions on inbound or outbound transfers, profit repatriation, or dividend distributions. SCSp partnerships benefit from the same freedom of capital movements, and profit remittances to non-resident partners are generally permitted without prior administrative approval. However, anti-money laundering and know-your-client obligations apply to all cross-border payment flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory requirement in Luxembourg to surrender export proceeds or to convert foreign currency receipts into euros within a set timeline. Export revenue may be held in any freely convertible currency in a bank account. Economic sanctions and EU restrictive measures may, however, impose blocking or reporting obligations in specific circumstances. No mandatory conversion ratio applies.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium with legal constraints. Digital Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) and payment institutions authorized in the EU/EEA may operate in Luxembourg under the EU PSD2 passporting regime, enabling account and payment infrastructure without a Luxembourg physical branch. However, tier-one commercial banks in Luxembourg often restrict initial account opening to in-country regulated banks and treat EMIs as unsettled or higher-risk counterparties. EMIs generally do not provide escrow-grade capital accounts for statutory or structuring purposes. An SCSp may use a fully licensed EU EMI for operational liquidity aggregation and settlement, but the primary corporate treasury account should be maintained with a fully licensed Luxembourg credit institution to preserve banking certainty and future fund financing credibility.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Most Luxembourg tier-one banks require at least one director or authorized signatory (beneficial owner) to appear for an in-person identity verification at the bank branch or at a notary or embassy-certified process. Remote opening has become partially possible post-COVID under CSSF guidance, but for non-resident SCSp structures with high-volume automated dropshipping flows, banks almost invariably demand a physical onboarding meeting for the general partner and the principal beneficial owner. A local professional (lawyer, fiduciary, or certified AML-compliance officer) cannot fully replace the physical interview unless the bank has approved the remote KYC procedure in writing. The account mandate may allow subsequent signatories to be added without physical presence once the initial account relationship is established.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume cross-border e-commerce flows with multiple third-party payment processors (Stripe, PayPal) and chargeback patterns typical of automated dropshipping
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan covering the automated dropshipping model, contractual agreements with suppliers and platforms, live platform analytics showing order flow and refund rates, a consolidated transactional projection matrix, and a comprehensive anti-fraud / chargeback mitigation policy provided to the bank during onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp pass-through vehicle with non-resident partners and no statutory minimum capital, posing a low substance risk perception
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Articles of association (contrat de société), registered office certificate, certificate of non-dissolution (récépissif), naming of the general partner, full beneficial ownership chain with passport copies and proof of residence for all partners, and an economic substance memorandum demonstrating that Luxembourg books, records, bank accounts, and decision-making functions exist for the SCSp.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual corporate payments paid to suppliers in Asia and to logistics fulfilment centers, triggering potential sanctions or trade-control screening
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master supplier agreements, export/import customs declarations (CN22/CN23 where relevant), copies of commercial invoices and waybills, logistic provider contracts, sanctions-screening certificate, and a written trade-control compliance policy covering embargoed goods and restricted parties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Credit transfers from or to payment processors (Stripe and PayPal) not established in Luxembourg, requiring assessment of AML wire-transfer transparency under EU Wire Transfer Regulation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Payment processor onboarding records, proof of the processors' authorization in their home EEA member state (or appropriate third-country licensing), updated settlement statements, a completed questionnaire on source and destination of funds, and a signed undertaking to provide ongoing transaction-level detail upon request.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections to a Luxembourg SCSp are executed by SWIFT MT103 from the investing partner's bank to the SCSp's Luxembourg-listed bank account. The beneficiary account should be titled exactly as the SCSp, and the payment reference must state 'Capital Contribution' or 'Equity Participation' in accordance with the SCSp partnership agreement. No specific Luxembourg purpose code exists; only the commercial description is legally required. Under EU anti-money laundering rules, the remitter and beneficiary details must include full names, account numbers, and legal identifiers. The bank may request the signed partnership agreement and the contribution schedule prior to accepting the inflow for tier-one onboarding compliance. For additional source verification, the bank will request a copy of the remitter's bank statement showing the originating account and the debit entry.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for dropshipping operations are settled through SWIFT MT103 for conventional bank transfers and through commercial letters of credit (L/C) for larger supplier orders requiring documentary protection. For supplier payments below EUR 50,000, a direct MT103 with supplier bank account details and invoice reference is standard. For high-value or recurring procurement, a confirmed irrevocable documentary L/C issued by the Luxembourg bank in favor of the supplier's bank provides settlement security. For intra-group treasury sweeps, an MT202/COV is used between banks. Clearing rails are TARGET2 for euro-denominated domestic payments and SWIFT for cross-currency settlements. In practice, most Luxembourg treasury retains euro and settles supplier payments via SWIFT in USD or CNY using spot conversion ordered through the primary relationship bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX forward contracts for EUR/USD, EUR/CNY and other trade-related currency pairs
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or non-convertible settlement currencies used for cross-border sourcing
Cross-currency swaps (XCS) for structural balance sheet hedging in connection with partner capital or dividend flows
FX options purchased for hedging of adverse exchange rate scenarios in trade settlement flows

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% at SCSp entity level (fiscally transparent); 24.94% aggregate Luxembourg CIT/ICC burden on corporate partners (17% CIT + 7% solidarity surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax in Luxembourg City)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp is not subject to Luxembourg CIT, municipal business tax or net wealth tax; participation exemption (100% exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains); unlimited loss carry-forward since FY2017 (0 = no statutory cap) with no carry-back; no IP box benefit for pure dropshipping trading income

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ACD annual partnership income-tax declaration (formulaire 500/510 series: SCSp transparency annex to the partner-level CIT return); e-filed through MyGuichet.lu / eTax with Luxtrust digital signature
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (CIT/ICC); monthly/quarterly VAT returns apply separately for the dropshipping activity
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 31 March of the year following the fiscal year-end (calendar year default); automatic administrative extension to 31 December for e-filing

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, RCS registration number, LEI, registered office in Luxembourg, corporate purpose, ISIC 4791 automated dropshipping code
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter Luxembourg address; list non-resident partners with foreign TIN and country code in the annex

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening and closing dates of the accounting period; default 1 January – 31 December
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners align their own fiscal year when declaring Luxembourg-source allocations

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full names, residence for tax purposes, tax identification numbers, contributions, profit-sharing ratios
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a TRC for each non-resident partner claiming treaty benefits; transparent allocation does not trigger Luxembourg dividend WHT

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable result of the SCSp: dropshipping revenue settled through Stripe/PayPal minus COGS, fulfilment, logistics, platform fees, chargebacks, and admin costs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners include only income attributable to a Luxembourg permanent establishment; pure remote dropshipping without Luxembourg activity creates no PE exposure

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of the taxable result to each partner according to the limited partnership agreement and LIR rules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Luxembourg assesses non-resident partners on their allocated share only when a PE exists or the SCSp carries out Luxembourg-source commercial activity

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of related-party transactions (supplier purchase prices, logistics, payment fees) and confirmation of arm's length margins
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Related-party suppliers must hold TP files in their own jurisdiction; the Luxembourg RTS is mandatory unless the entity qualifies as an SME

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation from commercial accounting profit to taxable profit: non-deductible expenses, notional deductions, off-balance payments, loss carry-forwards
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Show the share attributable to non-resident partners separately; the DTA credit is claimed by the partner, not by the SCSp

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly instalments paid, balance due, and credits; cross-reference to Luxembourg WHT certificates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners claim foreign tax credit relief in their state of residence; no refund claim lies at SCSp level

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Certification of completeness and accuracy by the Luxembourg authorized manager (gérant), date, e-signature
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only the Luxembourg manager signs; non-resident partners do not sign the Luxembourg return

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: administrative fine up to EUR 25,000 (AO s.168); default assessment surcharge of 10% of the tax due; late payment penalty interest at 0.6% per month; repeated non-filing and concealment can escalate to criminal tax fraud proceedings; RBE late-filing fines up to EUR 10,000

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% standard Luxembourg dividend WHT; 0% for distributions by the SCSp because it is fiscally transparent and without legal personality; 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for qualifying EU corporate shareholders; treaty rates 5%/10% apply where the SCSp is reclassified as opaque
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the beneficial owner submits a TRC and a beneficial-ownership statement to the Luxembourg paying agent; the Luxembourg payer files Form 105 with the ACD requesting authorization for the reduced rate before payment (or claims a refund); the claim is denied where the partner is a shell entity without substance; the SCSp must disclose the allocation in its annual transparency annex
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg domestic law imposes no WHT on outbound interest or royalties; dividends 15% domestic rate; under most DTAs interest is 0%–10% and royalties 0%–5%; payments from dropshipping platform settlement fees do not constitute royalties absent IP licensing

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg Master/Local File obligations arise for groups with consolidated turnover above EUR 50 million (SME definition: fewer than 250 employees and turnover not exceeding EUR 50 million or balance sheet not exceeding EUR 43 million); CbCR applies at EUR 750 million group turnover. The SCSp must evidence substance: Luxembourg registered office, Luxembourg bank/payment settlement, local manager, board/partner meeting minutes and commercial rationale. Absent substance, LIR s.6 GAAR, ATAD CFC rules and the EU Unshell/ATAD 3 proposals empower the ACD to reclassify the SCSp as opaque, deny treaty benefits, and impose 24.94% aggregate taxation plus penalties
